We cap the\n      // wrapper's width here so a long option wraps/gets cut off at the far edge instead.\n      const availableWidth = window.innerWidth - CONTENT_MARGIN * 2;\n\n      if (context.dir !== 'rtl') {\n        const itemTextOffset = itemTextRect.left - contentRect.left;\n        const left = valueNodeRect.left - itemTextOffset;\n        const leftDelta = triggerRect.left - left;\n        const minContentWidth = triggerRect.width + leftDelta;\n        const contentWidth = Math.min(availableWidth, Math.max(minContentWidth, contentRect.width));\n        const rightEdge = window.innerWidth - CONTENT_MARGIN;\n        const clampedLeft = clamp(left, [CONTENT_MARGIN, rightEdge - contentWidth]);\n\n        contentWrapper.style.minWidth = minContentWidth + 'px';\n        contentWrapper.style.left = clampedLeft + 'px';\n      } else {\n        const itemTextOffset = contentRect.right - itemTextRect.right;\n        const right = window.innerWidth - valueNodeRect.right - itemTextOffset;\n        const rightDelta = window.innerWidth - triggerRect.right - right;\n        const minContentWidth = triggerRect.width + rightDelta;\n        const contentWidth = Math.min(availableWidth, Math.max(minContentWidth, contentRect.width));\n        const leftEdge = window.innerWidth - CONTENT_MARGIN;\n        const clampedRight = clamp(right, [CONTENT_MARGIN, leftEdge - contentWidth]);\n\n        contentWrapper.style.minWidth = minContentWidth + 'px';\n        contentWrapper.style.right = clampedRight + 'px';\n      }\n","numLines":36,"startLine":816,"totalLines":1782}}}

Here's a summary.\n\n## The bug\n\nIn the `Select` pop-up's default `item-aligned` positioning (`SelectItemAlignedPosition.position()` in `packages/react/select/src/Select.tsx`), the content wrapper was given a `minWidth` but **no `maxWidth`**. When an option is wider than the screen:\n\n1. The wrapper grew wider than the viewport.\n2. The horizontal clamp `clamp(left, [CONTENT_MARGIN, rightEdge - contentWidth])` produced a **negative** `left`/`right` (because `rightEdge - contentWidth` went below the margin), shoving the pop-up off the left edge — that's the \"cut off on the wrong side\" look in the report.\n3. The un-capped width let the inner viewport (`overflow: auto`) scroll sideways.\n\n## The fix\n\n`packages/react/select/src/Select.tsx` — in the horizontal-positioning block:\n- Compute `availableWidth = window.innerWidth - CONTENT_MARGIN * 2` (the same band the existing clamp uses).\n- Cap `contentWidth` at `availableWidth` so the clamp pins the pop-up to the near margin instead of going negative.\n- Set `contentWrapper.style.maxWidth = availableWidth` so the wrapper never exceeds the screen; the long option then wraps within the box and the viewport no longer scrolls sideways.\n\nBoth the LTR and RTL branches get the identical treatment, so it's fixed in both locales.\n\nI also added a `LongOptionsNarrowScreen` story (LTR + RTL) that reproduces the scenario for manual/Chromatic verification.\n\nVerification: type-check passes for the Select package (the one reported error is a pre-existing unused-import in `Tooltip.test.tsx`, untouched by me), and ESLint is clean on both changed files.\n\nTracing the reported ~470px-wide screen: the pop-up now pins to `left: 10px`, caps at `maxWidth: 450px`, and the long option wraps to multiple lines — exactly the expected screenshot — with no horizontal scroll.\n\nOne note: there are no Jest unit tests for this package (positioning is measured via `getBoundingClientRect`, which jsdom stubs to zero), so this is covered by the story rather than a unit test.
